instrument: server/tools/test_run20_declared_production_changes.py + server/tools/production_tree.py (the byte-identical frozen-file guard over server/app/simulation/)

instrument: server/tools/test_run4_validate_seven.py::A2.8 and A3.2 band ladders; server/tools/test_run20_cycle11_parameter_provenance.py::line of balance boundary
what_the_instrument_did: Asserted, boundary by boundary, the four-band ladders of Look-Ahead Schedule Health and Contingency Burn Rate, and asserted that the line of balance separation boundary was visible to the parameter sweep. Run 4 had looked for a source for the first two and found none, and recorded that beside each band; the third was added when cycle 11 found its own sweep subtracting real boundaries from view.

resolution: THE LADDERS ARE GONE AND THE FIGURES STAY. The owner's supplied contract states in terms that no universal status bands are supplied for these quantities and that where the numerical method is correct but the bands are not calibrated the correct output is exposed with calibration pending. The band cases are replaced by checks the finding actually supports: each module's figure is asserted exact at the values the boundaries used to sit at, and NO colour may be asserted anywhere across that range. The line of balance check is restated on a boundary that still exists and was in the same swallowed set, so the property that the sweep subtracts nothing is still proved by a real case.

what_the_instrument_did: Required the overhead absorption rate to DECLARE the reported progress figure, on cycle 5's stated rule that a fact is not omitted because its consequences are inconvenient; required the inflation index and the overhead rate to be dependent because both scaled by progress; and required the Bayesian estimate at completion to be dependent on the earned-value readers. All three were true of the code as it then stood.
how_it_was_caught: Observed red against the v3 build at each of the three sites, with the declared fact sets printed beside the observed ones.
resolution: THE SAME RULE PRODUCES THE OPPOSITE ANSWER BECAUSE THE MODULES CHANGED. v3 absorbs overhead over an explicit allocation base and reads no progress figure; the inflation index reads a named external series and reads no progress figure; the Bayesian update reads a stated prior and a stated observation model and reads no earned-value field. Declaring the old facts would now assert dependences that do not exist, which cycle 5 recorded as the error that DID HARM. Each check is INVERTED rather than deleted, so a regression that reintroduced any of the three would turn it red, and each inversion is paired with a positive control that must still find a dependence where one genuinely exists.

what_the_instrument_did: Restored each mutated production file from the bytes captured before the injection and confirmed the restore by comparing SHA-256 digests. The digest matched every time.
how_it_was_caught: Fault F6's baseline came back RED after a restore the digest check had confirmed. The source on disk was correct and the behaviour was not: CPython had cached the compiled mutant, its cache is invalidated on the source's modification time and size, and an injection that replaces a line with one of similar length restored inside the same clock second changes neither.
resolution: The compiled cache for the touched file is dropped on BOTH sides of every injection, not only after the restore: the same staleness would otherwise let a mutant be written and the unmutated cache be executed, which would show a guard staying green and be recorded as a vacuous guard that is nothing of the kind. The campaign now reports 6/6 with every baseline green again after restore. Recorded here because a restore that fails while every byte-level check says it succeeded would have left a mutated analytical layer running under a green report.
